column1: • This sizing sheet is a standalone calculation. Inputs from other tabs within the workbook do not affect the final calculation.
• Deployment Model and Size sets the predefined values as determined by VCF Installer.
• Configure the Assumptions and Host parameters according to your preference. Appliance sizes are listed per appliance.

• The over-subscription ratio of 2:1 are designed to ensure a performant management domain for most deployments. Higher Ratios are supported. Regardless of the ratios you choose, you should monitor the platform continuously and add hardware if consistent performance bottlenecks are observed

• Select the principal storage as VCF 9.x Supports vSAN and Non-vSAN Storage in the Management Domain. vSAN Policy used for sizing calculation is determined on VMware recommended host count and not minimum.
• Add additonal vCPU, RAM or Disk requirements that may be required to accurately size the Management Domain.

• As each workload domain requires additional vSphere and, optionally, NSX components to be deployed, this tab allows you to correctly calculate the requirements for your management domain by selecting the intended number and profile of workload domains you plan to deploy.
• The management domain is mandatory and cannot be deselected. Its NSX Manager instance is required and can be shared with future workload domains.

• A maximum of four NSX Local Manager instances may be federated by a single NSX Global Manager instance. This includes inter-region and intra-region NSX Local Manager instances. Factor in this maximum when deciding whether to include Global Manager resources for a new workload domain.
• If VCF Operations already exists, then sizing input is not required for VCF Operations. Similar for VCF Automation.
• Cloud Proxy selection is automatic, if you are deploying VCF Operations or have an Exisiting VCF Operations.
• Components such as Software depot , LCM, Identity broker, SALT are enabled by default when deploying VCF service runtime on the first VCF Instance.
• Components Realtime Data, Software depot and Identity broker are configured within the VCFMS instance. No additional appliances are deployed.
• Real-time Metric, Log management, are enabled as part of day 2 deployment and are deployed within the VCFMS instance.
• Log management size should not be larger than the Instance Profile. The VCFMS cluster scales to accommodate the log management deployment.

• Software depot and Identity broker are deployed, sized by default in the First VCF Instance. Optional Software depots and Identity broker deployments can be sized for additional VCF Instances. vCPU and RAM requirements for these components are allocated from the existing VCFMS cluster.
• License Hub for vDefend and Avi is required if deploying Avi Load Balancers or Security Service Platform. A single License Hub is required per VCF Fleet.
• SSPI = Security Services Platform Installer; SSP = Security Services Platform; A single SSP installer can manage up to 5 SSP instances.

• The SSP form factor selection is based on the respective management or workload domain NSX Manager appliance size. A medium form factor is required to activate Security Intelligence. For a larger configuration and inventory scale, you must use the large or extra-large form factor.

• To activate all vDefend Advanced Threat Prevention capabilities, including Malware Prevention Service, Network Traffic Analysis, NDR Sensor, and Network Detection and Response, you need a large SSP form factor with at least 8 worker nodes.
